Committed by ADB to Turkmenistan in 17 public sector loans, grants and technical assistance, as of 31 December 2025

register.name: Procurement of health products for the control of infectious diseases, 2026–2027
register.detail: Ministry of Health and Medical Industry · with UNDP · 2026–2027 · fully funded by the Government of Turkmenistan
register.note: Follows the 2024–2025 agreement, with a budget above $34 million, signed on 3 May 2024
register.text: A health programme fully funded by the Government of Turkmenistan and run with UNDP, which buys the products for tuberculosis, HIV testing and reproductive health, safe blood transfusion and viral hepatitis B and C services. It takes over the Global Fund programme step by step so that it rests fully on domestic funding by the end of 2027, which carries the health standard.
by: Ministry of Health and Medical Industry

register.name: Supporting the Energy Transition for Remote Settlements in Turkmenistan
register.detail: GEF grant · signed 11 November 2026 at COP31, Antalya · five years · more than US$4.17 million · implemented by UNOPS with the Ministries of Environmental Protection and Energy
register.note: Up to 10 pilot solar mini grids of up to 2 MW in all, and feasibility work for 120 more settlements
register.text: A five-year grant of the Global Environment Facility, signed by the Government of Turkmenistan and UNDP, for remote settlements that depend mostly on diesel generators for their electricity. It builds up to ten pilot solar mini grids and prepares 120 more settlements for solar power, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Glaciers to Farms (G2F) Regional Program (FP283)
register.detail: GCF · approved 30 October 2025 · effective 8 January 2026 · US$250 million for nine countries, in two grants and one loan · accredited entity ADB · 2% disbursed
register.note: The GCF shows US$27.5 million of its financing for Turkmenistan, from this one project; total programme value US$3.5 billion with co-financing
register.text: A regional programme of the Green Climate Fund, led by the Asian Development Bank, for nine countries of Central and West Asia, Turkmenistan among them. It funds climate-informed planning, adaptation projects, resilience bonds and support to agricultural enterprises for more stable water and food supplies, which carries the water and food standards.

register.name: Exit of the National Tuberculosis Program of Turkmenistan from the Global Fund
register.detail: Global Fund grant · signed 26 December 2024 · runs 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027 · more than $6.2 million · UNDP as Principal Recipient
register.note: The Global Fund has invested more than $37 million in the national tuberculosis programme since 2010
register.text: A grant of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, signed by the Government of Turkmenistan and UNDP, to complete the move of the national tuberculosis programme to full domestic funding by 2027. It widens diagnosis, including mobile units in remote areas, secures essential medicines and moves patients to shorter treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis, which carries the health standard.
by: Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

register.name: Improving Nursing Quality and Capacity Project
register.detail: ADB loan · approved 25 September 2025 · loan agreement signed 11 November 2025 · €64.7 million ($75 million equivalent) · $2 million JFPR grant · $23 million from the government · total $98 million
register.note: ADB’s first health sector project in Turkmenistan, under its country partnership strategy for 2024–2028
register.text: An Asian Development Bank loan, with a grant from the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific, to increase the number and quality of nurses and midwives in Turkmenistan. It builds a new, climate-resilient Ashgabat Nursing School with simulation labs, equipment and modern curricula, which carries the health and education standards.
by: Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific

register.name: Three cancer treatment hospitals in Balkanabat, Turkmenabat and Mary
register.detail: IsDB · approved July 2024 · financing agreement signed 23 October 2024 in Washington · total project cost $259 million
register.note: Oncology services for 11,750 patients; the Ministry of Finance and Economy lists credit from IsDB and the Saudi Fund for Development for the centres in 2026–2028
register.text: An Islamic Development Bank financing agreement for three new hospitals specialised in cancer treatment, in the Balkan, Lebap and Mary provinces. They are to offer oncology services to 11,750 patients, with training for specialists, which carries the health standard.

items.name: Blind and Deaf Society of Turkmenistan
items.text: A public association that runs training and production enterprises for people with visual and hearing impairments, among them a cardboard and printing workshop in Ashgabat, re-equipped and opened in October 2023 to make more paper bags, cards and other printed goods, and sewing workshops in Mary and Turkmenabat.
